title: Lesson 75: Incident Response for Agents: Hallucinations, Data Leaks, Rollback, and Postmortems
description: The responder arc for an agent that acted while nobody watched: freeze the trace before rollback, roll back by action class and compensate where reversal is impossible, and run a blameless postmortem that ships a fix.

questions.question: Per the lesson "Incident Response for Agents", what must happen before any rollback, restart, or credential revocation when you confirm an agent incident?
options: Export or snapshot the incident window's trace tree to storage independent of the production system
Delete the affected sessions' logs so the bad behavior is not preserved
Revert to the last known-good prompt immediately to stop the bleeding
Restart the agent to clear its in-memory state before investigating
questions.explanation: The lesson: a rollback swaps the running version and a restart clears in-memory state, and either can overwrite or orphan the exact span-level record the postmortem needs. So you freeze or export the trace first, to storage independent of production, before any recovery action.

questions.question: The answer agent that made the mistake sent 40 incorrect refund emails to customers. Per the lesson's rollback-by-action-class framework, why is this class hard to roll back, and what is the correct substitute?
options: Emails are idempotent and can be reversed like a database write, so no follow-up is needed
A sent message cannot be unsent, so the response is a follow-up communication template, a legal review of that follow-up, and extraction of the impacted-customer list
The emails can be recalled because the agent has read access to the customer inboxes
Restarting the agent makes the sent emails untraceable so they can be ignored
questions.explanation: The lesson groups customer communications as the class where a sent message cannot be unsent. The rollback table specifies the substitute action: a follow-up communication template under legal review plus the impacted-customer list extraction.

questions.question: In the MTTD-for-Agents detection chain, if the entire fourteen-day delay before awareness sits between Signal and Trigger, what is the root cause you should fix, per the lesson?
options: Missing instrumentation on the agent's action path
Poor alerting hygiene, because the pager did not reach the operator
A tripwire that never fired on the signal
The human took too long to acknowledge the page
questions.explanation: The lesson maps each gap in the chain to its own root cause: a delay between Action and Signal is missing instrumentation, between Signal and Trigger is a tripwire that never fired, and between Page and Acknowledgement is alerting hygiene. Here the gap is Signal to Trigger, so the missing tripwire is the fix.
